summary: Reading the log: p= is the ansible-connection PID, u= the local user, the control socket line shows host:port and remote user, plus socket path, plugin and connection time. Port None means default; grep by PID.
questions: How do I read the Ansible network log?
What does port None mean in the network log?
How do I filter the log for one connection?

answer_card.title: Read the network log
answer_card.answer_md:
- `p=28990`: PID of the `ansible-connection` process
- `u=fred`: local user running Ansible (not the remote user)
- `creating new control socket for host veos01:22 as user admin`: host:port and remote user
- `control socket path is ...`: persistent socket location
- `using connection plugin network_cli`: persistent connection in use
- `connection established ... in 0:00:22`: time to get a shell

Port `None` means the default port. Filter with `grep "p=28990" $ANSIBLE_LOG_PATH`.
